- The first DER encoding of an ASN1Set not built in DER order, which includes every SET read by the parser, cached its copy of the elements before sorting it, so another thread encoding the same SET, or comparing it with equals(), at the same time could use the copy unsorted, or part way through the sort with some elements present twice and others missing, and so produce a wrong DER encoding - for example of a CMS SignerInfo's signed attributes when two threads verified the same SignerInformation at once. The copy is now cached only once it is sorted.

- A CMS AuthenticatedData message using the des-ede3-cbc or rc2-cbc CBC-MAC, as the CMSAuthenticatedDataGenerator javadoc example did, and carrying no authenticated attributes could have its first eight content bytes replaced without the MAC failing: the MAC started from the IV in the macAlgorithm parameters, which nothing covers when the MAC input is the content alone (RFC 5652 sec. 9.2), so one difference XORed into the IV and the first block left the MAC unchanged. JceCMSMacCalculatorBuilder now writes these MACs with a zero IV, which earlier releases also verify, and the generators, CMSAuthenticatedData, CMSAuthenticatedDataParser and RecipientInformation.getMac() refuse a non-zero IV for a message without authenticated attributes. Messages written by earlier releases in that form carry a random IV and can be read by setting org.bouncycastle.cms.allow_unauthenticated_cbc_mac_iv to true; messages with authenticated attributes are unaffected. The javadoc examples now use HMAC-SHA256.

- RecipientInformation.getMac() did not check the content-type authenticated attribute of a CMS AuthenticatedData message, so the eContentType could be changed without the MAC failing and a message whose authenticated attributes had no content-type attribute was accepted. RFC 5652 sec. 9.2 and 9.3 require the attribute whenever authenticated attributes are present and require its value to match the eContentType; getMac() now enforces both, as SignerInformation already does for SignedData.

+- Both PKIXCertPathReviewer copies (org.bouncycastle.pkix.jcajce and the deprecated org.bouncycastle.x509) let a delta CRL decide the status of a certificate. A delta CRL lists only the changes since its base CRL, so a certificate revoked on the base was reported as not revoked when the CRLs the reviewer was given held a current delta and only an expired base, or earlier deltas and no base at all, and the presence of a base was checked without reading it. SignedMailValidator gives the reviewer the CRLs carried in the signed message, so the holder of a revoked signing certificate could have a message accepted by including CRLs the CA had published. As in CertPathValidator, only a complete CRL now decides the status of a certificate, whether it is found in the CertStores or fetched from a CRL distribution point; where no current complete CRL is available the reviewer reports that rather than a status.

+- The PKIXCertPathReviewer copies did not refuse a CRL carrying a critical extension other than the issuing distribution point and the delta CRL indicator, as RFC 5280 sec. 5.2 requires and CertPathValidator does, and looked up a certificate on an indirect CRL by serial number alone, taking the first entry with that serial whichever certificate issuer it named. Such a CRL is now refused, and the entry is matched on the certificate issuer as well, as CertPathValidator has done since github #2464.
